novelty_flags.one_line: The survey misses AssaadEtAl2024 (UAI 2024), the closest published causally-sufficient SCG total-effect identification and adjustment result; it does not subsume the latent-confounded kernel, but requires an explicit separation and comparator boundary.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv v2, 19 May 2025; corroborating version because the cited TMLR OpenReview PDF is access-gated
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives sufficient SCG-front-door conditions and a do-free formula for latent-confounded micro total effects, rather than a complete procedure.
The paper studies total-effect identification from extended summary and ordinary summary causal graphs, provides necessary-and-sufficient SCG conditions and adjustment sets, under causal sufficiency.
The paper bounds the graph segment needed to decide ID for a fully specified latent-confounded causal time-series graph, with dependence on width and maximum lag.

source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 1943-1944, semi-Markovian model definition and identifiability definition; abstract
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper works with recursive semi-Markovian models and gives complete identification and graphical nonidentifiability characterizations for fixed causal diagrams.
The paper gives a sound-and-complete conditional-effect identification algorithm for a PAG representing a finite Markov-equivalence class.
The paper gives complete SCG identifiability and finite adjustment sets for linear direct effects under no hidden confounding.
The paper distinguishes macro from micro queries and establishes soundness and completeness of do-calculus for macro total effects in latent-confounded SCGs.
The paper defines the modified-Bartlett HAC estimator, proves positive semidefiniteness, and states its consistency regime including bandwidth o(T^(1/4)).

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add Assaad, Devijver, Gaussier, Goessler, and Meynaoui (UAI 2024) and formalize the separation: causally sufficient adjustment completeness versus latent-confounded semi-Markovian fixing completeness; add a theorem or corollary recovering its applicable subcase.
Give a worked non-front-door latent-confounded input with an explicit finite state encoding, a transducer trace, and either a compiled cylinder functional or serialized lag-switch certificate.

Strengthen the comparator result to separate the method from both Assaad's latent-confounded front-door theorem and the UAI-2024 causally-sufficient total-effect adjustment criterion on a parameterized family, not one isolated input.
